notes: No command channel exists. Pugstorm ships no RCON, no admin HTTP API and no interactive console for the Core Keeper dedicated server: it is a Unity headless build launched with -batchmode -logfile, so its own stdout goes to CoreKeeperServerLog.txt and stdin is not a command pipe. The Pelican/Pterodactyl egg confirms this shape - it starts the binary with -batchmode -logfile CoreKeeperServerLog.txt, tails that log for output, and its stop action is ^C (SIGTERM), not a console command. Moderation is done either from a client that is an admin (Esc > player list / Manage Players, click the red cancel symbol to kick or ban, and the Banned Players section to unban) or by stopping the server and editing JSON: Admins.json holds {index, privileges, name, steamId} entries (privileges 2 = first/full admin, 1 = added in-game) and PlayerBans.json holds a banList of {index, name, steamId, crossPlatformId, stringId}. Nodecraft states explicitly that PlayerBans.json keys on SteamID64, not character name; crossPlatformId/stringId are used instead for non-Steam (crossplay) accounts, so the lineIdPattern here only pulls Steam bans. Both files live under the server's DataPath, which defaults to a DedicatedServer subfolder of the normal Core Keeper save location (~/.config/unity3d/Pugstorm/Core Keeper/DedicatedServer on Linux, the equivalent Unity LocalLow folder on Windows) and can be relocated with the -datapath launch argument; most hosts surface it as a DedicatedServer folder next to the install. Edits require a server restart to take effect. Sources disagree only in that several hosting blogs publish generic /kick, /ban or /op chat commands for Core Keeper; those are from mods, not the base server, and one hosting wiki (supercraft.host) explicitly warns against presenting them as built-in and states there is no published RCON port or admin-command set. No official Pugstorm page documents any console command, so this file records transport "none" rather than inventing one.
